method: scripts/strategy_lab.py was run four times in throwaway copies of the checkout (git archive HEAD, then the seeded inputs swapped back to their published state: manifest and availability from d51ac43, the results log frozen at 183 games from main @ d320fea). The published data/app/lab.json was never written; each leg wrote lab.json inside its own copy. Leg A = the engine exactly as published, seeded inputs. Leg B = the same seeded inputs with only the NF-90 name-join fix applied. Leg C = the fixed engine on the refreshed inputs (the manifest as repointed by this session, log extended to 188), run twice.
engine_input_published: data/app/official_injuries_2026-11-14_0415AM.json (+ slate 1114_1117, ratings 1114c, players 1114c, results log frozen at 183 games, main @ d320fea state)
engine_input_refreshed: data/app/official_injuries_2026-11-15_0615AM.json (+ slate 1115_1118, ratings 1115, players 1115, log 188 games - the log extension is itself part of this refresh)

canonical_adoption.note: The refreshed build is adopted as canonical: the committed data/app/lab.json is exactly leg C's output (same engine, same manifest-named inputs), which is what the CI drift gate re-proves on every push.

seeded_reproduction.note: Leg A reproduces the lab.json committed at main @ d320fea (read via git show, so the proof stays stable once the refreshed build is adopted) byte for byte: same engine, same inputs, same rounding. It proves the pre-refresh artifact is exactly what the published engine produces.

determinism.note: The refreshed engine run twice on the same inputs produced identical bytes.

fix_effect.note: Leg B differs from leg A only by the NF-90 name-join fix. The vacated-minute fields change on exactly the team-sides whose listed players appear in the captured minutes table (on the seeded 11/14 report: MEM via Jerome and MIN via Edwards); no price field and no line-level availability field moves, so the fix cannot change an originated line. This is the field-level proof of the claim made in the engine comment.

refresh_effect.note: Leg C differs from leg B by the input refresh: the window rolled (5 finals left, 12 games on 11/18 entered), every team's official advanced ratings moved after the 11/14 finals, and the newest report replaced the day-old one. Every price-field move on a shared game traces to those documented input deltas.

verdict: invariance holds where it must: the seeded artifact reproduces byte for byte with the published engine, the refreshed engine is deterministic, and the name-join fix moves no price field. Lines are still injury-blind by design (F-1823b910-03 / S-1823b910-03 owner decision open); the refresh moves prices only through ratings and rest.
